notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput & strict latency SLOs — replace existing ad-hoc self-hosted endpoints.
Primary KPIs: 99th pctl latency < 120ms for short-chat (<=1024 tokens), sustained 600K tokens/min across peak windows, cold-start under 800ms.
Workload shape: mix of low-latency chat (60% requests, avg 180 tokens), heavy reranking & embeddings pipelines (30% batch jobs), nightly bulk index updates (10%).
Model preferences: leaning to open Llama2-70B-Chat variant trimmed to 16k/32k context, also testing 4-bit quantized LLMs for cost. ask: can Redwood host quantized variants with same SLA?
Quantization convo: Pelago prefers Q4_0/Q4_K_MIXED for baseline; concerned about latency variance and hallucination risk. Wants Redwood's perf profile by quantization level.

Context length: need up to 64k in some legal summarization flows but majority at 8k. Request: model variants pinned by max_ctx in routing policy, fallback to shorter context model when capacity constrained.
Batching & KV cache: require per-tenant KV cache warmup policy and prefix caching for repeated system prompts. Ask: ability to tune batch size ceiling per model to maintain 99th pctl latency SLO.
Throughput guarantees: procurement pushing for committed baseline throughput (tokens/sec) and credits for throttling events. Negotiating SLA credits and runbook response times.
Reserved GPU planning: initial ask 4x A100 (p4d equivalent) dedicated with autoscale to +2 for burst. Want guidance from Redwood on headroom formula — currently using conservative 40% safety margin.

SLA specifics: uptime target 99.95% for dedicated endpoints, 1-hour incident acknowledgement, 4-hour remediation for P2. Pelago requests rollback/fallback policies and documented multi-region failover in contract.
Security & compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS (customer-managed keys), detailed audit logs exported to SIEM, and quarterly compliance reviews.

Proof-of-concept: agreed POC scope — 72h synthetic load + replay of 24h production traces. Success criteria: hit token throughput target, meet 99th pctl latency target for chat, KV cache hit rate >70% for repeated flows.
Quote feedback: finance asks to model ARR impact vs on-prem baseline; want cost per 1M tokens and cost for reserved pool of 4 GPUs + autoscale buffer
Notes from call: 'If Redwood can show deterministic 99th pctl under our trace replay, procurement will greenlight reserved capacity' — VP Eng (quote).
Open technical questions: cold-start behavior for new model variants, how pre-warming can be scheduled, telemetry export granularity (per-request tokens + batching metadata).
Internal Pelago constraint: legal requires data residency in us-east & eu-west only; cannot allow logs to be stored in APAC region without explicit approval.

Suggested Redwood actions: provide quantization perf matrix (latency & quality deltas), recommended reserved GPU sizing by model & ctx_len, draft SLA language for committed throughput and fallback routing
